browser.definizione: The program you use to visit websites, such as Chrome, Safari, Firefox or Edge.

archiviazione-locale.definizione: A small space the browser reserves for each website to save data on your device. The data stays only in that browser and on that device.

cloud.definizione: Real computers, sitting in a company's data centers, that you use over the internet without having them physically in front of you.

github.definizione: A website where people who develop software keep, share and work on their projects, including together with others.

codespaces.definizione: A GitHub service that gives you, in a few seconds, a ready-made computer in the cloud to use inside your browser.

hardware.definizione: The physical part of a computer: everything you can touch, such as processor, memory, disk, screen and keyboard.

software.definizione: The set of instructions that tell the hardware what to do: programs, apps, operating systems.

processore.definizione: The component that executes programs' instructions. It can have several cores working in parallel.

memoria-ram.definizione: The fast memory where the computer keeps the data it is working on right now. It empties when the computer turns off.

disco.definizione: The component that keeps data and programs even when the computer is off. Today it's usually an SSD, an electronic memory.

sistema-operativo.definizione: The software that manages the hardware and makes it available to other programs in an orderly and safe way, such as Linux, Windows or macOS.

kernel.definizione: The heart of the operating system: it talks directly to the hardware, and every program has to go through it to use processor, memory and disk.

linux.definizione: A free Unix-style kernel; by extension, the operating system built around it. It's the system containers were born on.

distribuzione.definizione: A complete operating system based on the Linux kernel, with its own programs and settings, such as Ubuntu or Debian.

programma.definizione: A set of instructions saved on the disk, ready to be executed.

processo.definizione: A running program: it uses processor and memory, it starts when you launch it and ends when it finishes or you close it.

pid.definizione: Process IDentifier: the unique number the kernel assigns to each process to recognize it.

file.definizione: A set of data saved on the disk with a name, such as a photo, a document or a program.

cartella.definizione: A container for files and other folders, used to keep them tidy.

file-system.definizione: The way the operating system organizes files and folders. On Linux it's a tree that starts from the root /.

applicazione.definizione: A program, or a set of programs, designed to do a job for people.

libreria.definizione: A set of already-written functions that programs can use instead of rewriting them from scratch.

dipendenza.definizione: A library or program an application needs in order to work, often in a precise version.

versione.definizione: The number that identifies a published state of a piece of software, for example 2.4.1 (major.minor.patch).

terminale.definizione: The window where you type commands and read the computer's answers, text only.

shell.definizione: The program running in the terminal that reads the commands you type and starts the programs requested. It's also a programming language.

bash.definizione: The most common shell on Linux. The name stands for Bourne-Again SHell.

prompt.definizione: The text at the start of the line, such as studente@corso:~$, telling you the shell is waiting for a command and showing user, computer and folder.

comando.definizione: A line that asks the shell to start a program, in the form: command options arguments.

opzione.definizione: A part of the command that changes its behavior. It starts with one dash (-l) or two (--all).

argomento.definizione: A part of the command that says what to work on: a file, a folder, a piece of text.

manuale.definizione: A command's official documentation, opened with man command-name. Exit with q.

cartella-corrente.definizione: The folder the shell is in right now: commands work there unless told otherwise. pwd shows it.

cartella-personale.definizione: The folder where each user keeps their own files, such as /home/studente. The shell writes it as ~.

percorso-assoluto.definizione: A path that starts with / and starts from the root of the file system: it works from any folder.

percorso-relativo.definizione: A path that doesn't start with / and starts from the current folder. .. means the folder above.

cronologia.definizione: The list of commands already typed, which the shell remembers. Bring them back with the up arrow; the history command shows them all.

completamento.definizione: The shell feature that, when you press Tab, finishes typing command, file and folder names.

utente.definizione: An identity used to work on the computer: it has a name, a number (UID), a home folder and owns files. Users are listed in /etc/passwd.

gruppo.definizione: A set of users, used to give them all the same permissions on certain files.

root.definizione: The administrator user (UID 0): it passes every permission check and can do anything on the system.

sudo.definizione: The command that runs a single command as root, after asking for the user's password.

permessi.definizione: The rules saying who can read (r), write (w) and execute (x) a file: three triplets for owner, group and others. Shown by ls -l and changed with chmod.

script.definizione: A text file containing a series of commands to run in order. It's started with ./name if it has execute permission.

pacchetto.definizione: An archive containing a program ready to install, with its version and list of dependencies.

gestore-pacchetti.definizione: The program that downloads, installs, updates and removes packages, resolving dependencies. On Debian and Ubuntu it's APT (the apt command).

repository.definizione: An online archive of packages, run by the people who maintain a distribution, from which the package manager downloads programs.

variabile.definizione: A name associated with a value, created in the shell with NAME=value and used with $NAME.

variabile-ambiente.definizione: A variable that is part of a process's environment and is passed to the programs it starts. Created with export; Docker sets it with -e.

path.definizione: The environment variable listing, separated by colons, the folders where the shell looks for programs.

standard-output.definizione: The channel where a program writes its normal results. Redirected with > and passed to another command with |.

standard-error.definizione: The channel, separate from standard output, where a program writes error messages. Redirected with 2>.

redirezione.definizione: Sending a command's output to a file instead of the screen: > overwrites, >> appends, 2> is for errors.

pipe.definizione: The | symbol connecting two commands: the first one's standard output becomes the second one's input.

segnale.definizione: A short message sent to a process asking it to do something, for example to terminate: TERM asks it to close, KILL ends it immediately.
